hook_text: Gogo is seventy-eight, alone, and her phone is flat. If she falls at night, who hears her? Here is how a design brief turns that question into something you can build.
clip_script: Investigate: who, where, when, what. Gogo, slow, weak hands, bed, stove, toilet in the yard, a neighbour across the fence, no alarm company. Ask her: reachable, pressable, works in the dark and in load shedding, stoppable, no monthly fee. Brief in three parts: problem, users, purpose, a few sentences, naming the need and never the circuit. Specs, testable: any one of three buttons, big and low, loud and bright, battery, glow, reset, a year of standby. Constraints: the kit, two hundred rand, low voltage, two sessions, weatherproof, documented. The circuit earns its place next week.
visual_style: Whiteboard house plan with three button icons; a speech bubble of Gogo's requests; a three-box brief; two columns labelled specifications and constraints filling in.
pacing: Scenario, user voice, brief, specs, constraints.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write Gogo's brief in your own three sentences.
